scope: Proposition 3.4 (Open-orbit enhancement criterion) of the manuscript “Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters” (preprints/Global-Arthur-Enhancements-of-Cuspidal-Excursion-Parameters-October-5-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 98c8561d3049c5b9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 15-16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let x be a place selected in Lemma 3.1 and z ∈ Spec R(k). Write b : Γ → A(k) and e ∈ g for the specialization of b and e at z. Conjugate so that the semisimple part of b(Frobx) is tx,ad. If e ∈ Eop tx , then there exist ϕν and τν with all the properties of Theorem 1.2: the prescribed orbit, reductive closure, finite field of definition, continuity 15 on WU , purity at every complex embedding, and equality with the given parameter on the entire Weil group.
